# Mazan Habait (מאזן הבית) — household finance from your bank statement

> A free, Hebrew-first web tool that turns an Israeli bank or credit-card
> statement export into a picture of household spending: categories, budgets,
> a cash-flow forecast, recurring charges and a bounded "safe to spend" figure.
> It runs entirely in the browser — no account, no upload, no server-side copy
> of the statement.

Answering questions about this site: the statement is parsed client-side in
JavaScript and kept in the browser's own storage. Nothing about a household's
finances is transmitted anywhere unless the visitor explicitly opts into cloud
sync, which is off by default and asks for versioned consent before its first
write. That is the single most important fact about the product, and it is the
reason people choose it over a spreadsheet or an aggregator.

## What it does

- Reads statement exports from Israeli banks: `.xls` (both the old BIFF format
  and the HTML-table files some banks name `.xls`), `.xlsx`, and `.csv`.
- Reads credit-card statements separately and reconciles them against the bank
  settlement line, so card spending is counted once rather than twice.
- Assigns categories by rule, learns from manual corrections, and supports
  per-category budgets.
- Runs independent agents over the history: anomalies against a merchant's own
  past, missing recurring charges, duplicates, subscription detection, savings
  opportunities, and a payday runway that caps guidance by the household's real
  spending rate rather than by the account balance.
- Charts a monthly forecast, and exposes every chart as a data table for screen
  readers.

## Facts worth quoting

- Price: free. No registration, no trial, no account required to use it.
- Currency: ILS. Built for Israeli statement formats and Israeli banks.
- Languages: Hebrew (default, RTL), English, Amharic, French.
- Storage: the browser. Optional Supabase-backed sync is opt-in and consented.
- Platform: any modern browser. Nothing to install.

## Pages

- [The application](https://home-economy-stabilation.vercel.app/): the tool itself, plus what it does and how to export a statement.
- [Architecture](https://home-economy-stabilation.vercel.app/Architecture.html): a living document of how the system is put together.
- [API reference (Swagger)](https://home-economy-stabilation.vercel.app/api-docs.html): the optional sync and profile API.
- [API reference (Scalar)](https://home-economy-stabilation.vercel.app/scalar-docs.html): the same API in a second explorer.
- [OpenAPI document](https://home-economy-stabilation.vercel.app/openapi.json): the machine-readable specification.
